tasks.short: Monitor patients and report abnormal reactions

steps.what: Monitor patients' conditions and reactions throughout the imaging procedure
Report abnormal signs to the physician and follow immediate response instructions

tasks.design: Retain direct observation and existing patient-monitor use in {OTHER}, the patient-monitoring system. Abnormal signs still trigger immediate human escalation; a new dashboard or generated summary does not replace that response.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recognising a meaningful reaction requires clinical observation in context.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing monitors already support observation; no new labour-saving capability is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: A patient can deteriorate without a simple threshold breach.
tasks.human_edge: Notice distress, clarify symptoms and escalate promptly.
tasks.altitude: Patient observation and escalation responsibilities stay unchanged.

reach.task: Receive a concise account of an abnormal reaction
reach.learn: Clinical escalation and accurate symptom communication

evidence.claim: Existing patient-monitor readings supplement rather than replace direct observation and urgent escalation; no saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is technologist monitoring and reporting, excluding physician assessment and treatment. Their work remains unchanged outside the denominator.

Technologist observes the patient in s1 and reports observations in s2 with full time retained. Existing monitor sensors produce readings under the current clinical process; no new structured abnormal-sign flag, transcription or data capture is required. Unclear readings use existing clinical escalation.

Native monitor capabilities are considered first. Zero incremental upkeep because no change is introduced; existing monitor runtime earns no labour saving. Local clinical delegation remains unchanged.
research_questions: Where does the current escalation process delay clinical acknowledgement?

incremental.description: Unchanged monitoring and escalation add no upkeep

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 and upkeep 0. Routine observation and abnormal reactions retain all technologist time; existing monitoring runtime is not a saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Enter and verify scan commands and acquisition data

steps.what: Check patient, imaging request and authorised protocol requirements
Key scan sequences, commands and acquisition data into the imaging console
Verify staged settings and apply authorised adjustments or image capture commands

tasks.design: Use approved native protocol presets in {OTHER}, the imaging console, to reduce repeated parameter entry. The technologist still verifies patient and request, selects the appropriate authorised preset, checks every staged setting and personally applies acquisition commands.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated manual entry of standard acquisition settings.
tasks.enabler_now: Scanner protocol libraries support reuse of approved settings.
tasks.still_hard: Patient-specific changes and scanner differences require competent review.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when the standard preset does not fit this patient or request.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated keying; acquisition and clinical authority stay unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve a request needing a nonstandard acquisition protocol
reach.learn: Protocol indications, local limits and escalation

build_days.consent_and_access: 3-7 including clinical governance and device access

evidence.claim: Siemens teamplay Protocols supports distribution of scanner protocols; this does not establish autonomous patient-specific protocol selection.
Reuse of approved console presets can reduce repeated keying where it is not already used.

assumptions: Boundary covers console data and command entry, excluding patient positioning, the scan's existing machine runtime and diagnostic interpretation.

Referring clinician produces the existing imaging request with patient identifier, requested exam and clinical question. Protocol owner supplies versioned approved settings under the existing governance process. Technologist checks patient, request, scanner compatibility and applicable preset in s1 with full time retained; selection, manual exceptions and missing parameters remain in s2's 50%. Missing or incompatible presets use existing manual entry and clinical escalation.
Test native presets first. No free-text model chooses or composes protocols. Current permissions and clinical delegation apply, and any changed preset is revalidated before use.
unknowns: How much preset reuse already exists
Scanner compatibility and local protocol governance
research_questions: Do approved presets reduce keying after all selection and setting checks?

already_counted.description: Select preset, check staged parameters and handle manual exceptions

incremental.description: Check changed preset versions and report mapping issues

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient and request association, protocol revision and staged acquisition settings checked before applying; any change requires recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=82.5; gross 17.5 less upkeep 2 gives net 15.5. High assumes repeated manual keying today; low assumes native presets already cover most cases. Request and final setting checks retain 65 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check current work status and gather facts needed for coordination
Coordinate work with clerical personnel and other technologists or technicians

tasks.design: Configure a native worklist view in {OTHER}, the radiology information system, to reduce repeated status lookup. The technologist checks whether the displayed facts are current and retains the discussion that resolves constraints and handovers.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated navigation between existing work and readiness records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views can show already-recorded status together.
tasks.still_hard: Readiness can change before the record is updated, and work conflicts require dialogue.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a displayed status does not match the patient's actual situation.
tasks.altitude: Less status navigation with unchanged colleague coordination.

reach.task: Resolve a scheduling or readiness discrepancy
reach.learn: Status definitions and clear handover ownership

evidence.claim: A native imaging worklist view can consolidate existing records for review; no measured saving or automatic readiness decision is established.

assumptions: Boundary covers technologist status lookup and coordination, excluding clerical entry, clinical preparation and colleague time.

Imaging administrator produces existing appointment and exam identifiers and status; responsible clinical staff produce existing readiness records as part of unchanged care. No new fields or capture work are imposed on them. Technologist checks identity, timestamp and uncertainty in retained s1 time. Missing or stale status is clarified directly, never inferred as ready.
Test native worklist configuration first. No new automated prioritisation or staff scoring; existing runtime earns no saving.
unknowns: Latency and ownership of readiness records
research_questions: Does the consolidated view save lookup time after checking stale or incomplete status?

already_counted.description: Check status currency and clarify missing facts

incremental.description: Maintain view fields and report status mismatches

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=90; gross 10 less upkeep 2 gives net 8. High assumes duplicate screen navigation; low assumes stale status consumes the gain. Coordination retains 75 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assign radiologic staff duties to maintain patient flow

steps.what: Review patient flow, staff competence, availability and equipment constraints
Prepare the duty board from checked constraints and proposed assignments
Assign duties, communicate responsibilities and adjust for changing patient needs

tasks.design: Use a native duty-board template in {OTHER}, the radiology information system, to reduce copying of checked roster and worklist details. The authorised technologist chooses and communicates every assignment; no algorithm ranks staff or chooses clinical priorities.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated copying of staff and worklist facts onto a duty board.
tasks.enabler_now: Native board templates can reuse existing fields while retaining human assignment.
tasks.still_hard: Competence, workload, patient acuity and equipment changes need situated judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Balance patient needs and staff capability without reducing care to throughput alone.
tasks.altitude: Less duty-board copying with unchanged assignment authority.

reach.task: Resolve a staffing constraint that threatens safe patient flow
reach.learn: Competence boundaries and fair workload allocation

evidence.claim: A native duty-board template can reuse existing roster details while leaving assignment judgement human.

assumptions: Boundary is the technologist's duty assignment where delegated, excluding creation of the staff roster, competence assessment and execution of duties. Keep this preparation separate from general colleague coordination in roll-up.

Roster owner supplies existing staff availability; competence owner supplies authorised qualifications; clinical staff maintain existing worklist and equipment state. Their capture remains unchanged outside this task. Technologist checks currency and captures constraints in s1 with full time retained, and manually selects proposed duties in retained s2 time. Missing competence or status information requires clarification, not a default assignment.
Test native board configuration first. No behaviour-based allocation, staff performance scoring or automatic duty publication. Clinical delegation and employee consultation remain local requirements.
unknowns: Native board reuse and existing data coverage
research_questions: Does board reuse save copying time after constraint checks and manual assignment selection?

already_counted.description: Choose proposed duties and check reused board fields

incremental.description: Maintain board fields and exception handling

approvals.approved_version: Exact staff-to-duty board with current constraints checked before communication; any reassignment needs a fresh human check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=92; gross 8 less upkeep 2 gives net 6. High assumes duplicate board copying; low assumes live changes consume reuse gains. Constraint review and communication retain 80 hours.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technologist retains patient observation, acquisition checks and staff decisions while reducing repeat keying and lookup.
reach: Help radiologists resolve protocol exceptions and imaging supervisors address safe staffing constraints
role.ambitious_version: Maintain safe imaging flow with clearer records and full human control of clinical actions.
